description: Run a script on Linux instances to create symbol details for volatility 3

AccessKeyId.description: (Required) AccesskeyID to store evidence details in S3.

SecretAccessKey.description: (Required) SecretAccessKey to store evidence details in S3

SessionToken.description: (Required) SessionToken to store evidence details in S3.

SubscriptionManagerUsername.description: (Required) Username register to RHEL subscription manager

SubscriptionManagerPassword.description: (Required) Password register to RHEL subscription manager

runCommand: #!/bin/bash
# Like the Amazon Linux documents this fails loudly. A silently missing or
# unusable symbol table makes every later memory investigation on this kernel
# abort, weeks after the build that was reported as successful.
# Upstream versions, pinned. An unpinned clone builds whatever is at the tip of
# the default branch on the day of the incident - into the tooling that produces
# and reads forensic evidence. These match the pins already used by the
# acquisition and investigation documents so that one release means one set of
# tool versions. Note 504ensicsLabs/LiME redirects to jtsylve/LiME, its original
# author; cloning the old path works only while GitHub honours that redirect.
DWARF2JSON_REF=v0.9.0
set -o pipefail
fail() { echo "SYMBOL_BUILD_FAILED: $1" >&2; exit 1; }
cd /tmp
mkdir -p forensic-symbol-builder
cd forensic-symbol-builder
# Both values are quoted. Unquoted, a password containing a space, a
# semicolon or a $(...) broke the command or ran as root, and the
# credentials were visible to anything that could read ps.
sudo subscription-manager register --username '{{SubscriptionManagerUsername}}' --password '{{SubscriptionManagerPassword}}' --auto-attach
sudo subscription-manager config --rhsm.manage_repos=1
sudo yum install -y -q git go
# python3.8 resolves to the python38 module stream, which Red Hat retired in
# May 2023 and froze at 3.8.17. python3.12 is the full life cycle Python
# application stream in RHEL 8 (shipped from 8.10); python3.11 retired in
# May 2026 and is only a fallback for hosts still on RHEL 8.8 or 8.9.
sudo yum install -y -q python3.12 || sudo yum install -y -q python3.11
sudo subscription-manager repos --enable=rhel-8-for-$(uname -m)-baseos-debug-rpms --enable=rhel-8-for-$(uname -m)-appstream-debug-rpms
sudo yum install -y -q kernel-debuginfo-$(uname -r) kernel-debuginfo-common-$(uname -m)-$(uname -r)
git clone --depth 1 --branch "$DWARF2JSON_REF" https://github.com/volatilityfoundation/dwarf2json.git || fail "dwarf2json clone of $DWARF2JSON_REF failed"
echo 'clone done'
cd dwarf2json || fail 'dwarf2json source tree missing'
sudo go build || fail 'dwarf2json build failed'
echo 'dwarf2json build done'
vmlinux=/usr/lib/debug/lib/modules/$(uname -r)/vmlinux
test -f "$vmlinux" || fail "debug vmlinux not found for $(uname -r); check that the debug repositories were enabled"
symbol_file=$(uname -r).json
./dwarf2json linux --elf "$vmlinux" > "$symbol_file" || fail 'dwarf2json symbol generation failed'
# The redirect creates the file before dwarf2json can fail, so presence proves
# nothing. Require populated maps plus what volatility3 actually reads:
# symbols.linux_banner.constant_data, which is the only thing automagic can
# match an ISF to a capture with (see framework/automagic/symbol_cache.py),
# init_task to walk processes, and the task_struct definition. The path goes in
# through argv rather than through the program text.

python3 -c 'import json,sys; d=json.load(open(sys.argv[1])); s=d.get("symbols") or {}; b=d.get("base_types") or {}; u=d.get("user_types") or {}; banner=(s.get("linux_banner") or {}).get("constant_data"); sys.exit(0 if (s and b and u and banner and "init_task" in s and "task_struct" in u) else 1)' "$symbol_file" || fail 'the generated symbol table is not a usable volatility3 ISF file'
echo 'symbol build done'
# Why AWS credentials arrive as document parameters rather than an instance role:
# these are short-lived STS session credentials, minted per acquisition by the
# forensic Lambda with a session policy scoped to this case's S3 prefix - not
# long-lived IAM access keys. The host this runs on cannot be given an instance
# profile for the evidence bucket: it is either the machine under investigation,
# whose configuration must not be changed mid-incident, or an analysis host that
# must not hold standing access to other cases' evidence. Do not copy this
# pattern into a workload where an IAM role is available.
export AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID={{AccessKeyId}}
export AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY={{SecretAccessKey}}
export AWS_SESSION_TOKEN={{SessionToken}}
export AWS_DEFAULT_REGION={{Region}}
# AWS CLI v2 from the official archive, not `pip3 install awscli`: that
# installs the deprecated v1 package at whatever version the index serves.
curl -fsSL -o /tmp/awscliv2.zip https://awscli.amazonaws.com/awscli-exe-linux-x86_64.zip && unzip -q -o /tmp/awscliv2.zip -d /tmp && sudo /tmp/aws/install --update
aws configure set default.s3.max_concurrent_requests 20
aws s3 cp "$symbol_file" "s3://{{s3bucket}}/volatility3/symbols/$symbol_file" || fail 's3 upload of the symbol table failed'
echo s3 copy complete
ls -ltr
exit 0;
